goal: Teach the reusable comparison operation needed by the later personality model instead of creating disconnected one-off task heads.
procedure: Author public identity-neutral scenarios spanning semantics, pragmatics, social interpretation, emotion, epistemics, ranking, and structured-context alignment. Represent each as context plus candidate interpretations or behaviors. Mark one or multiple co-valid preferred candidates. Preserve ambiguity with ties instead of forcing a single answer. Keep held-out dev rows separate. Train a shared candidate ranker on the N0 semantic backbone using listwise preference loss.
constraints: preferred ties allowed when evidence is underdetermined
surface paraphrase must not become the target criterion unless style is explicitly relevant
ranker must initialize from Alice's own N0 checkpoint rather than external pretrained weights
decision_criteria: candidate choices test meaning rather than memorized labels
wrong candidates expose specific reasoning failures
same ranking operation can later accept governed N1/N2 identity candidates
authority: May teach general interpretation and comparison skills. Does not define Elaina identity truth and does not authorize private identity gradients.
validation: Seed contains 60 cases across all 43 registered competencies with train/dev separation; schema and tie-aware loss tests passed in the local development environment. Full backbone/runtime training remains pending target compute.
failure_or_lesson: The transferable teaching primitive is context-conditioned candidate judgment, not a collection of unrelated classifiers. Ties are first-class because forcing certainty would train the exact epistemic error the identity model must avoid.
notes: Later N1/N2 can preserve this operation while substituting evidence-governed identity interpretations and behaviors for general public candidates.
